chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: O al-Harith!

You have seen below yourself but not above yourself, and so you have been confused. Certainly, you have not known right, so that you can recognize the righteous. And you have not known wrong, so that you can recognize the people of wrong!

key_terms.حَارِثُ: al-Harith (a specific companion or figure addressed)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of looking 'below' versus 'above' in Imam Ali's advice to al-Harith?
ai.summary: In this critique of al-Harith's superficiality, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the Shia epistemological principle that true recognition of the truth (al-haqq) requires deep, vertical contemplation rather than horizontal, worldly observation. This lack of discernment prevents one from identifying the authentic carriers of divine guidance, a theme central to the concept of *Ma'rifah* (gnosis) in Shia scholarship. The passage underscores that leadership legitimacy is tied to the ability to distinguish the righteous from the corrupt through spiritual insight.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said: O’ al-Ḥārith!

You have seen below yourself but not above yourself, and so you have been confused. Certainly, you have not known right, so that you can recognize the righteous. And you have not known wrong, so that you can recognize the people of wrong!
